title: Satellite Image Classification
text:
← Back to projects
This project explores how deep learning can automate land-cover classification from multispectral Sentinel-2 satellite imagery. The convolutional neural network (CNN) distinguishes vegetation from non-vegetation. Such methods can support environmental monitoring, agricultural analysis and urban planning by reducing the need for manual image interpretation. This demonstration illustrates binary patch classification, not a complete monitoring system.
98.37% reported test accuracy · 27,000 dataset images · 2,700 test images

Interactive demo
Choose an example image and run the trained model directly in your browser.







NoteAbout the model





The CNN uses red, near-infrared and NDVI inputs from EuroSAT-MS. The reported accuracy comes from a random held-out test split and does not establish geographic generalisation. Demo images may overlap the training data. The model groups entire patches, rather than assigning a land-cover class to each pixel.
Dataset: EuroSAT (Helber et al.).

title: Martin Preiß
text:
Political Science | Data Science


Martin Preiß





I am a political scientist with a Master’s degree in Political Science from the University of Freiburg and an academic background in political science and theology. My research interests lie at the intersection of political science and data science, with a particular focus on political behaviour and quantitative empirical research. In my Master’s thesis, I examined the determinants of electoral participation by comparing classical statistical methods with machine learning approaches using survey data from the GESIS Panel.


I am interested in the application of computational methods to social and political phenomena and the methodological challenges associated with their integration into social science research. My broader research interests include political communication, the transformation of digital public spheres, the ethical and political implications of artificial intelligence and the role of emerging technologies in international relations. Through my academic work and independent programming projects, I aim to further develop my expertise in computational social science and interdisciplinary research.

title: Research
text:
Master’s Thesis



Master’s Thesis · 2026


Welche Faktoren erklären Wahlbeteiligung? Ein Vergleich erklärender statistischer mit explorativen Machine-Learning Ansätzen am Beispiel der Bundestagswahl 2017


Martin Preiß


Department of Political Science · University of Freiburg



Abstract


This thesis examines voter turnout in the 2017 German federal election using data from the GESIS Panel Core Studies. A theory-driven logistic regression model with 12 predictors is compared with two exploratory machine learning models, Random Forest and XGBoost, trained on 222 predictors.


All three models identify previous electoral participation, voting norms and political interest as central predictors. Machine learning additionally reveals patterns related to media consumption and political trust, while offering modest improvements in predictive performance. The findings highlight the complementary role of explanatory and predictive modelling in political science.
